paper_title: Controlling Molecular Doping in Organic Semiconductors

knowledge_points.content: Molecular doping in organic semiconductors occurs via two distinct mechanisms: ion pair (IP) formation, characterized by integer charge transfer, and charge-transfer complex (CTC) formation, characterized by fractional charge transfer and molecular orbital hybridization.
knowledge_points.evidence: Neutral molecular dopants are understood to interact with OSCs by two mechanisms: ion pair (IP) formation and charge-transfer complex (CTC) formation... In an IP, there is integer (or nearly integer) charge transfer... In the OsC/dopant CTC, there is fractional charge transfer between the OsC and dopant.

knowledge_points.content: The conductivity of P3HT doped with F4TCNQ exhibits a threshold doping ratio of approximately 2 × 10⁻⁶, below which conductivity decreases and above which it increases superlinearly at high doping levels (>3%).
knowledge_points.evidence: Figure 2 shows that the conductivity of the semiconducting polymer poly(3-hexylthiophene) (P3HT) initially decreases with the addition of F4TCNQ until reaching a threshold doping ratio of about 2 × 10⁻⁶... eventually becoming superlinear at high doping levels (> 3%).

knowledge_points.content: Fourier transform infrared spectroscopy (FTIR) can quantify the degree of charge transfer in F4TCNQ-doped systems by measuring the redshift of the C≡N vibrational stretch; a full ionization results in a shift of 33 cm⁻¹ (from 2227 cm⁻¹ to 2194 cm⁻¹).
knowledge_points.evidence: In samples of neutral F4TCNQ, the C≡N stretch occurs at 2227 cm⁻¹. If F4TCNQ is fully ionized to F4TCNQ⁻, the C≡N stretch redshifts 33 cm⁻¹ to 2194 cm⁻¹... this shift has been reported to be linear with the degree of charge transfer.

knowledge_points.content: The electron affinity (EA) of the common p-type dopant F4TCNQ is approximately -5.24 eV, while the stronger organometallic dopant Mo(tfd)₃ has an EA of approximately -5.6 eV.
knowledge_points.evidence: we used the UPS measurements of -5.24 eV for F4TCNQ and -5.6 eV for Mo(tfd)3 measured by the Kahn and co-workers as a reference

knowledge_points.content: The formation of IPs versus CTCs depends significantly on the host structure; for example, the polymer P3HT forms IPs with F4TCNQ, whereas its structurally similar oligomer quaterthiophene (4T) forms CTCs with only 0.21 electrons transferred.
knowledge_points.evidence: P3HT/F4TCNQ forms an IP while 4T/F4TCNQ forms CTCs... In the 4T/F4TCNQ sample, the peak shifts only 7 cm⁻¹ to 2220 cm⁻¹ indicating a charge transfer of 0.21 electrons.

knowledge_points.content: The Salzmann unified model for doping incorporates the Hubbard U (on-site Coulomb interaction) to explain why the ionization energy (IE) increases when an electron is removed from the dopant or OSC, contradicting simpler models that ignore electron-electron interactions.
knowledge_points.evidence: The revised model accounts for the on-site Coulomb interaction, a term commonly known as the Hubbard (U)... Critically, this revised model correctly explains why the IE value increases when an electron is removed.

knowledge_points.content: The choice of casting solvent affects doping efficiency in P3HT:F4TCNQ films; films cast from chloroform exhibit higher doping efficiency and stronger π-π stacking compared to those cast from chlorobenzene.
knowledge_points.evidence: Muller et al. looked at the effect of casting solvent on doping efficiency... observing stronger π-π stacking and higher doping efficiency in films cast from chloroform as opposed to chlorobenzene (CB).

knowledge_points.content: Doping efficiency in P3HT nanofibers is morphology-dependent, with J-aggregate nanofibers showing more than 10 times higher efficiency than H-aggregate nanofibers due to increased hole delocalization.
knowledge_points.evidence: They observed > 10× higher doping efficiencies in j-aggregate nanofibers, which were interpreted as resulting from increased hole delocalization due to the more planar backbone.

knowledge_points.content: Air-stable n-type doping can be achieved using metal sandwich dimers that are stable during solution processing and only cleave to form the active, air-unstable dopant species upon the doping reaction.
knowledge_points.evidence: A recent innovation to address air instability was the use of metal sandwich dimers that cleave upon doping. The dimers can be solution processed and only generate the air-unstable dopant after the cleavage reaction.

knowledge_points.content: Atomic iodine is an problematic p-type dopant for organic semiconductors because its low barrier to sublimation leads to rapid diffusion out of the film, causing device instability and cross-contamination.
knowledge_points.evidence: the low barrier to sublimation made the use of I2 for doping problematic because even at room temperature it rapidly diffuses through and out of the films... iodine vapor leaving the film can contaminate other samples.

knowledge_points.content: The energy of an ion pair in a doped organic semiconductor is stabilized by the Madelung energy (electrostatic energy), which depends on the degree of charge transfer and the separation distance between the electron and hole.
knowledge_points.evidence: it was realized that the Madelung energy (electrostatic energy) of the ionized state acts to stabilize the IP... E(δ) = (IE - EA)δ - k (e²/r) δ²
